title: Why a Bar Beats a Spot

scenes.tts: Spots of light often did little in cat visual cortex. So why would a bar at the right angle do better?
scenes.visual: On-screen text: Why does a bar at the right angle beat a spot?
scenes.narration: Spots of light often did little in cat visual cortex. So why would a bar at the right angle do better?

scenes.tts: David Hubel and Torsten Wiesel recorded single cells in the visual cortex of anaesthetized cats.
scenes.visual: A simple line drawing, nothing graphic: a cat facing a screen, with an electrode symbol over the back of the head. Label: Hubel and Wiesel, cat V1.
scenes.narration: David Hubel and Torsten Wiesel recorded single cells in the visual cortex of anaesthetized cats.

scenes.tts: An electrode just outside one cell counted its spikes, while light was projected onto a screen.
scenes.visual: Close-up schematic: the electrode tip beside one neuron. A spike raster, without audio, ticks below. A projector beam lands on the screen.
scenes.narration: An electrode just outside one cell counted its spikes, while light was projected onto a screen.

scenes.tts: Spots often did little. A slit or bar of light at the right angle drove some cells hard.
scenes.visual: A spot on the screen: the raster stays sparse. A bar at the right angle: the raster runs densely.
scenes.narration: Spots often did little. A slit or bar of light at the right angle drove some cells hard.

scenes.tts: For cells that answered small spots, they mapped the field spot by spot. In the cells they called simple cells, the field split into on and off subregions.
scenes.caption: For cells that answered small spots, they mapped the field spot by spot. In the cells they called simple cells, the field split into ON and OFF subregions.
scenes.visual: Small spots flash one at a time across a field; each leaves a green or magenta mark. The marks build a map. Label: simple cell.
scenes.narration: For cells that answered small spots, they mapped the field spot by spot. In the cells they called simple cells, the field split into ON and OFF subregions.

scenes.tts: The subregions are long and narrow, side by side. A common layout is a narrow on strip with an off strip on each side.
scenes.caption: The subregions are long and narrow, side by side. A common layout is a narrow ON strip with an OFF strip on each side.
scenes.visual: The map resolves into a green vertical strip between two magenta strips.
scenes.narration: The subregions are long and narrow, side by side. A common layout is a narrow ON strip with an OFF strip on each side.

scenes.tts: Picture the field as a grid of squares with made-up values. Plus and minus are balanced, as they roughly are in many real simple cells.
scenes.visual: The strips become a grid six squares tall: the centre column of six green squares each marked +1, a column of six magenta squares on each side, each marked −0.5. Small label: numbers made up for teaching; ON total equals OFF total. The sum meter appears beside it with a dashed line labelled: threshold 2 (made up). Small note: this toy cell has no spontaneous firing.
scenes.narration: Picture the field as a grid of squares with made-up values. Plus and minus are balanced, as they roughly are in many real simple cells.

scenes.tts: Which will win: a small spot on the on strip, or a bar lying along it?
scenes.caption: Which will win: a small spot on the ON strip, or a bar lying along it?
scenes.visual: On-screen text: Small spot on the ON strip, or a bar along it?
scenes.narration: Which will win: a small spot on the ON strip, or a bar lying along it?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: The bar wins by a wide margin. It lands on plus all along the strip. The spot collects only a little.
scenes.visual: A one-square spot lights: the meter shows +1 and stays below the threshold line; rate 0. Then a bar lights the whole green column: the meter shows +6, fills past threshold, rate 4 (arbitrary units), and the raster runs hard.
scenes.narration: The bar wins by a wide margin. It lands on plus all along the strip. The spot collects only a little.

scenes.tts: This made-up cell fires only when the sum clears its threshold. The spot falls short. That is one reason spots often did little in cortex.
scenes.visual: The dashed threshold line on the meter is highlighted, labelled threshold 2 (made up); the +1 bar sits below it. Small note: real simple cells could still give weak responses to spots.
scenes.narration: This made-up cell fires only when the sum clears its threshold. The spot falls short. That is one reason spots often did little in cortex.

scenes.tts: Now turn the bar. It leaves the on strip and lands on both off flanks, and the sum falls to near zero.
scenes.caption: Now turn the bar. It leaves the ON strip and lands on both OFF flanks, and the sum falls to near zero.
scenes.visual: The bar rotates over the grid. As it crosses, it covers one green and two magenta squares; the meter falls toward 0 (on screen: +1 − 0.5 − 0.5 = 0). Beside it, an orientation tuning plot with its axis running 0 to 180 degrees, labelled bar orientation, draws a single peak as the bar turns.
scenes.narration: Now turn the bar. It leaves the ON strip and lands on both OFF flanks, and the sum falls to near zero.

scenes.tts: Now light the whole field at once. What does the cell do?
scenes.visual: On-screen text: Light over the whole field?
scenes.narration: Now light the whole field at once. What does the cell do?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: Plus and minus cancel, so diffuse light does little.
scenes.visual: The whole grid lights. On screen: +6 − 6 = 0; rate = max(0, 0 − 2) = 0 (arbitrary units). The meter sits at zero and the toy cell's raster is empty.
scenes.narration: Plus and minus cancel, so diffuse light does little.

scenes.tts: A bar along one off strip gives a negative sum. This toy cell is already silent. A cell with spontaneous firing would slow down.
scenes.caption: A bar along one OFF strip gives a negative sum. This toy cell is already silent. A cell with spontaneous firing would slow down.
scenes.visual: A bar lights one magenta column: on screen, −3. The meter drops below zero and the toy cell's raster stays empty. Beside it, a second raster labelled: a cell with spontaneous firing, whose slow ticks thin out while the bar is on.
scenes.narration: A bar along one OFF strip gives a negative sum. This toy cell is already silent. A cell with spontaneous firing would slow down.

scenes.tts: So orientation selectivity is not a separate property. To a first approximation, it comes from the shape of the field.
scenes.visual: Caption card: To a first approximation, orientation selectivity comes from the shape of the field.
scenes.narration: So orientation selectivity is not a separate property. To a first approximation, it comes from the shape of the field.

scenes.tts: Make the strips longer but keep them just as narrow. Now the sum falls faster as the bar turns, so tuning is sharper.
scenes.visual: Two fields side by side with strips of equal width, one short and one long. Label: width held fixed. Beside each, an orientation tuning curve on an axis from 0 to 180 degrees: the long-strip curve is narrower. No numbers.
scenes.narration: Make the strips longer but keep them just as narrow. Now the sum falls faster as the bar turns, so tuning is sharper.

scenes.tts: The threshold sharpens tuning further. Measured spike tuning is narrower than the field's sum alone predicts.
scenes.visual: A broad curve labelled sum, with a horizontal threshold line across it. Only the part above the line is shaded and redrawn as a narrower curve labelled spikes.
scenes.narration: The threshold sharpens tuning further. Measured spike tuning is narrower than the field's sum alone predicts.

scenes.tts: How might such a field be built? Hubel and Wiesel suggested geniculate cells with on centres in a row, all exciting one cortical cell.
scenes.caption: How might such a field be built? Hubel and Wiesel suggested geniculate cells with ON centres in a row, all exciting one cortical cell.
scenes.visual: Round LGN centre-surround fields slide into a vertical row over the field; arrows from each converge on one cortical neuron.
scenes.narration: How might such a field be built? Hubel and Wiesel suggested geniculate cells with ON centres in a row, all exciting one cortical cell.

scenes.tts: That cell gets an elongated on strip. Their surrounds could add off flanks, and off-centre cells beside the row could strengthen them.
scenes.caption: That cell gets an elongated ON strip. Their surrounds could add OFF flanks, and OFF-centre cells beside the row could strengthen them.
scenes.visual: The row of green centres merges into the green ON strip; their magenta surrounds fade into the OFF flanks. A few OFF-centre LGN fields, magenta centres, line up beside the row and join the flanks.
scenes.narration: That cell gets an elongated ON strip. Their surrounds could add OFF flanks, and OFF-centre cells beside the row could strengthen them.

scenes.tts: They offered this as a suggestion. Recordings in the nineteen nineties supported the aligned input. Exactly how the flanks are built is less settled.
scenes.caption: They offered this as a suggestion. Recordings in the 1990s supported the aligned input. Exactly how the flanks are built is less settled.
scenes.visual: Label over the wiring diagram: proposed 1962. Aligned, sign-matched LGN input supported by 1990s recordings. Full circuit not settled.
scenes.narration: They offered this as a suggestion. Recordings in the 1990s supported the aligned input. Exactly how the flanks are built is less settled.

scenes.tts: So a bar beats a spot because it collects plus all along the on strip. A spot collects only a little.
scenes.caption: So a bar beats a spot because it collects plus all along the ON strip. A spot collects only a little.
scenes.visual: The aligned bar and the small spot sit side by side on two copies of the grid, each with its meter: one full, one barely raised.
scenes.narration: So a bar beats a spot because it collects plus all along the ON strip. A spot collects only a little.
